claims.text: The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a density of 10.21 g/cm³.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
The proposed intervention is to replace 10%, 20%, or 30% of the Hf content with V.
V is sufficiently lighter than Hf to lower the mass density when substituted for Hf.
Partial replacement of Hf with V will reduce the density of HfMoTaTiZr by approximately 10–15%.
The V-modified alloy will retain at least 90% of the baseline room-temperature yield strength.
The V-modified alloy will retain at least 90% of the baseline yield strength at 1000 °C.
The modified alloy will maintain a BCC solid-solution phase.
Adequate atomic-size mismatch and sluggish diffusion will stabilize the BCC solid solution after V substitution.
V substitution will preserve the beneficial lattice distortion present in the baseline alloy.
Preserving lattice distortion and the solid solution will preserve strengthening at room temperature and 1000 °C.
The room-temperature yield strength of the modified alloy will be at least approximately 1440 MPa.
The yield strength of the modified alloy at 1000 °C will be at least approximately 770 MPa.
V substitution will cause only a minimal compromise in ductility.
Mechanical performance should be evaluated under tensile loading at room temperature and tensile or compressive loading at 1000 °C.
V substitution may produce undesirable secondary phases or microstructural changes that impair ductility or long-term stability.
Excessive V substitution may compromise solid-solution strengthening.

contradictions.description: The uncertainty field states that an optimum substitution level must be determined and that excessive V may degrade strengthening, whereas the falsification rule rejects the overall hypothesis if any one of the 10%, 20%, or 30% variants fails a threshold. Failure of a deliberately non-optimal level therefore invalidates a hypothesis that otherwise allows level-dependent performance.

The high-temperature loading mode is not fixed consistently: the conditions and measurements allow tensile or compressive testing, while the design specifies tensile testing. Tensile and compressive yield strengths are not necessarily interchangeable.
